mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of periods with declining FEDFUNDS for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances with UNRATE > 4.5% for two months, or Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising federal funds rates and falling unemployment rates indicates monetary tightening amid strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with strong labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances with FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE falling, or interaction term Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, housing starts (HOUST) below 1,300,000 units signal weakening demand for housing, which precedes slowing economic growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances with HOUST < 1300.0 during late-cycle, or Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past 3 months indicates weakening manufacturing activity that reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of periods with declining INDPRO for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When year-over-year CPI inflation exceeds 3.0%, it signals accelerating price pressures that prompt aggressive monetary tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances with CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising housing starts (HOUST) and falling industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a sectoral shift toward housing demand, which typically boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances with HOUST rising and INDPRO falling, or interaction term Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle defined by FEDFUNDS above 2.0% with rising 3-month moving average, the S&P 500 typically underperforms, producing negative returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced liquidity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances with FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising 3m MA, or Rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.
